items.item: column mapping is enabled by setting delta.columnMapping.mode to name
the protocol specifies two modes, by name and by id; Delta Lake 2.1 and below do not support id mode

The table in examples.py is plain CSV text, not Parquet/Iceberg/Delta's real binary formats — disclosed in the script's own module docstring and FACT-CHECK.md red-team #1 and #2. What transfers is the real mechanism (field-ID projection, logical-to-physical name mapping), not either format's actual on-disk layout.

Part 2's 'without column mapping' demo assumes the physical column name always equals the logical name, which is Delta's real behavior before column mapping is enabled — a sourced distinction (the mapping doc's own text implies this), not an invented contrast, per FACT-CHECK.md red-team #3.

at.step: Reveal: without column mapping, a rename really does rewrite the file

items.item: This topic does not demonstrate type widening or nested-struct evolution with real code, only rename/reorder/add — type widening and defaults are covered via Iceberg's own sourced default-value rules rather than a fabricated demo for every sub-claim, consistent with this chapter's established pattern within a 10-step/15-minute budget.

Enabling Delta column mapping is an irreversible, protocol-upgrading operation per the docs' own warning — this topic's demo builds two separately constructed tables (with and without mapping) rather than demonstrating a live migration, which is out of scope for this topic's budget.

The rename-plus-insert schema change reproduced here (cust_id -> customer_id renamed, region inserted before amount_cents) is the identical change topic 3's own examples.py used for plain Parquet, now reproduced at the table level on a real on-disk file, directly answering topic 3's own corruption with the table-format fix, as CHAPTER.md's own visual idea for this topic specifies.

at.step: Reveal: reproduced for real — position-based matching corrupts the table

items.item: Delta's column mapping feature is documented as 'currently experimental with known limitations' as of Delta Lake 1.2.0+ — this topic treats it as Delta's real, current mechanism, not a claim it is stable-forever or default-on.
This topic does not cover snapshot lifecycle, time travel, or garbage collection — that is explicitly the next topic's subject, and this topic's own handoff names that boundary.
The prerequisites panel lists topic 3 and topics 10-15 as declared background, matching CHAPTER.md's own stated prerequisites-panel note for this topic.

Both the Iceberg-style and Delta-style demos in examples.py are pure in-memory logic plus small deterministic local file I/O with no timing assertions, verified identical across 3 consecutive runs — no flaky-timing risk of the kind topics 14 and 15 had to specifically design around.

items.item: Delta's rename-without-rewrite demo verifies the claim by comparing the data file's raw bytes before and after the rename, not just checking the final schema — a stronger, more literal verification of 'without the need to rewrite the underlying Parquet files' than inspecting metadata alone.
